implementation: The writer identity setup now calls a shared-helper-based projection for source-bound AC1012/AC1014 LAYOUT graphs targeting R2000. It validates one source identity per retained BLOCK_RECORD, stages reciprocal layout handles in a copy, preserves selected extension-dictionary identities, and leaves the caller and source unchanged on refusal. The earlier legacy validation still refuses export before this setup is reached.
controls: Two locally authored AC1012 resaves and a regenerated AC1014 resave pass the bound source proof and direct writer-identity projection. Each associated layout is linked to the matching writer identity while all source BLOCK_RECORD layout handles remain zero.

Wrong target, modified or duplicate writer identities and modified source layout associations refuse without changing the complete caller identity vector; restoring the source and retrying succeeds. An explicit selected extension-dictionary override survives projection.

Existing source graph, viewport, ASCII/binary destination preservation, missing-input and trusted-adapter retry controls pass. Five focused graph and adapter CTests pass; separate R2000–R2013 ASCII/binary generated output passes physical and ezdxf checks.
limits: This stage is not reached by an ordinary legacy export while the existing refusal is active. It is not an end-to-end staged-output, proxy CLASS, native AutoCAD or semantic qualification.
The extension-dictionary override is a writer-identity control, not independent proof of an arbitrary extension graph.
